localHook: Canyon Lake is a gated lakefront community, not a typical suburb—and water damage here plays by different rules. Aging copper plumbing in 1970s and 1980s tract homes, seawall seepage after heavy rain cycles, dock-adjacent moisture that never fully dries, boathouse mold that builds quietly over a season. Gallagher Restoration has been the first call for homeowners around Holiday Harbor, East Bay, and the private coves for over 15 years. We work alongside the Canyon Lake POA and local property managers regularly—so access coordination, gate protocols, and HOA documentation requirements are familiar ground, not a surprise. This is home. Every job inside these gates carries the weight of a neighbor doing right by another neighbor.

neighborhoods.heading: Every corner of Canyon Lake, gates included
neighborhoods.intro: From the main lake estates to the quieter inland streets, we respond throughout the community.

items.name: Holiday Harbor
items.body: Lakefront and dock-adjacent homes here see recurring moisture intrusion at foundation lines. We’ve responded to more water calls in Holiday Harbor than any other Canyon Lake enclave—seawall weeping and aging copper supply lines are the usual culprits.

items.name: East Bay
items.body: East Bay’s 1970s–80s construction stock means galvanized and early-copper plumbing that is reaching the end of its service life. Pinhole failures and slow slab leaks are common—and often go unnoticed until flooring buckles or mold appears behind cabinetry.

items.name: Main Lake Estates
items.body: Larger lakefront properties carry more exposure—longer plumbing runs, boat-dock ice machines, exterior structures prone to mold in shaded corners. We work these properties with the scale and documentation that estate owners and their insurers expect.

items.name: Private Coves & Inland Streets
items.body: Canyon Lake’s interior residential streets still carry the fire-smoke and mold risks common to all Inland Empire communities. Proximity means we’re here before the damage spreads.

commonDamage.heading: What damages Canyon Lake homes most
commonDamage.intro: Geography and housing age create a predictable damage profile here. These are the calls we take most often.

items.title: Seawall seepage and foundation moisture
items.body: Lakefront properties absorb lateral moisture through aging seawalls and foundation cracks. Left untreated, it saturates subfloor assemblies and produces chronic mold. Early intervention—moisture mapping, targeted extraction, and controlled drying—stops the cycle before structural repair becomes necessary.

items.title: Aging copper and galvanized plumbing failures
items.body: Homes built in the 1970s and 1980s are entering or past the typical 40–50-year service window for copper supply lines. Pinhole leaks, joint failures, and sudden pipe bursts are all active risks. We dry affected assemblies completely to prevent secondary mold growth.

items.title: Dock and boathouse mold
items.body: Boathouses and dock structures stay humid year-round. Mold colonizes wood framing, fiberglass panels, and stored equipment faster than most owners expect. Our IICRC-trained crews remediate these spaces and document the work for insurance and POA compliance.

items.title: Ice machine and appliance leaks
items.body: Dock ice machines and built-in appliances are a persistent water source in lakefront homes. A slow supply-line leak behind a refrigerator or under a boathouse sink can saturate subfloor and wall cavities for weeks before discovery.

pricing.heading: Honest numbers on restoration cost
pricing.body: Assessment is free—no charge to show up, evaluate the damage, and give you a clear picture of scope. Most residential restoration jobs in Canyon Lake fall between $500 and $15,000 depending on the category of damage, the materials affected, and how long the moisture was present before discovery. Water mitigation alone runs lower; jobs that include mold remediation, structural drying of lakefront assemblies, or post-fire restoration run higher. If you have homeowners insurance, Gallagher works directly with your carrier. We prepare the documentation adjusters need and handle the back-and-forth so the process moves faster. You’re not left translating between a contractor and an adjuster while your home sits wet.
